summary: The 2D screening label is not_2d_applicable, and Studio did not run (simulation status: skipped). The gate failed on Studio input validity: the custom_2d_steady experiment has an empty floorplan and no power_w, while the schema requires 1-128 blocks plus a power object. input_gate_pass and scientific_gate_pass are false, simulation_allowed is false, comparison_valid is false, and the result is not independently verified. Because of the gate, the final verdict is no simulation and no numerical comparison. No exact replication is claimed. The paper scenario is WaFFLe on a 16-tile, 32nm 2D CMP using gem5, McPAT and HotSpot 6.0, with LLC way-gating plus per-core fine-grained DVFS. The headline observable is an 8.4 C maximum reduction in peak temperature versus the paper's own baseline (6.2 C for average temperature) on the 8MB LLC. This is a relative reduction from a transient, policy-driven workload. The paper's temperatures were sampled at 0.33 us with way-shutdown at 2M-cycle intervals. A custom 2D steady run would have no transient trace and cannot reproduce this dynamic behavior. No pinned Ascend910 or ATPlace commit, bundled EV6/GCC adaptation, or generated placement was used, so there is no illustrative input.flp or one-row input.ptrace and no source commit to report. The artifact search found no linked code, configs or floorplans. The paper gives no block geometry or per-block watts, and the only stated boundary condition is a 47 C ambient. Studio's package and cooling defaults would differ from the unpublished HotSpot configuration. Any such run would be illustrative only. Numerical comparison would require matching location (hottest on-chip point), aggregation (maximum across nine apps), regime (transient with leakage feedback) and boundary assumptions, and none of these can be matched. At most, a qualitative statement is possible: lowering power during memory stalls and gating cache ways plausibly reduces temperature and leakage. This is not verified here.
limitations: Studio did not run; there are no simulated temperatures to assess.
The experiment has an empty floorplan and no power_w, so the input is invalid.
The paper publishes no block coordinates, dimensions or per-block wattages; the floorplan came from HotFloorPlan and appears only in figures. Digitizing it would be speculative.

The reported 8.4 C and 6.2 C are temperature reductions versus the paper's own baseline, as maxima across nine PARSEC apps. They are not absolute temperatures, so they cannot be matched against a Studio absolute result.

The paper's behavior is transient and policy-driven (2M-cycle way gating, ns-scale DVFS switching, 0.33 us thermal intervals, temperature-dependent leakage). A steady 2D run with a one-row trace cannot capture it.
The HotSpot 6.0 package, TIM, spreader, heat sink and convection settings are unpublished; only the 47 C ambient is known. Studio defaults would differ.
Regulator powers (0.106/0.168 W) and stall energies (337 nJ) are not block powers and cannot be turned into a power map.
The Fig. 20 labels (373.83 K, 366.59 K) have uncertain units and association, so they cannot serve as a quantitative benchmark.
No code, configs or supplementary assets were found, and there is no pinned Ascend910/ATPlace or EV6/GCC source commit or placement assumption to report.

The paper's workload is transient and dynamic. Cache ways are gated at 2M-cycle intervals, per-core DVFS switches during memory stalls at ns scale, and temperature is traced at 0.33 us. A steady 2D thermal runner with a one-row power trace cannot reproduce this time-varying behavior.

The controller and optimizer (way-shutdown and FG-DVFS algorithms, directory-based miss detection, performance/IPS feedback) are architectural policies. Their effect depends on gem5 and McPAT performance and power traces, which are not available in a Studio thermal solve.

The paper publishes no block coordinates, dimensions, or per-block wattages. The floorplan is generated by HotFloorPlan from McPAT areas and is shown only as tile figures (Fig. 13, Fig. 20) and temperature maps. No same-scenario block geometry and power rows can be built from the paper without digitizing or inventing values.

The reported observable is a temperature reduction relative to the paper's own baseline, not an absolute temperature. It depends on HotSpot 6.0 package and cooling parameters that the paper does not publish except for a 47 C ambient. Studio package and cooling assumptions cannot be matched, so temperatures are not numerically comparable.

Dynamic power gating of LLC ways is modeled as a time-varying change in power and leakage with temperature feedback (component-wise leakage from the previous period's temperature). A static Studio power map has no such coupling.
The paper is a 2D tiled CMP with no 3D stacking, interposer, or chiplets. This is a mismatch with 3D and interposer thermal tools but not a blocker for a 2D scenario.

No complete experiment is extractable, so the floorplan is empty. If an illustrative run were made, any generated 2D placement and one-row power trace would be separate from paper facts, and its temperatures would not be compared numerically to the paper.
Studio package and material properties (die, TIM, heat spreader, heat sink, convection) are bundled defaults and not the paper's HotSpot 6.0 configuration, which is not published.
Ambient is the only paper-stated thermal boundary condition (47 C, Table 1, PDF p.13). Other boundary conditions would be Studio defaults.
